microtheory.name: law_jurisprudence
microtheory.definition: Law + legal philosophy. Legal systems (common law, civil law, religious law, customary law). Constitutional, criminal, civil, international branches. Jurisprudence schools: natural law (Aquinas, Finnis), legal positivism (Bentham, Austin, Hart, Kelsen, Raz), legal realism (Holmes, Llewellyn), critical legal studies, Dworkin's law as integrity. Substrate analogue: the formal admissibility grammar + procedure governing collective enforcement of norms.

concepts.name: law_definition
concepts.definition: System of rules enforced through institutions. Hart: union of primary (conduct) + secondary (recognition, change, adjudication) rules. Substrate analogue: substrate's admissibility grammar Γ.

concepts.name: rule_of_law_jurisprudence
concepts.definition: Government bound by law equally applied. Distinct from rule by law (instrument). Prospectivity, generality, clarity, publicity, stability, non-contradiction, possibility of compliance — Fuller's eight.

concepts.name: rights
concepts.definition: Legal or moral entitlements. Hohfeld's four: claim, privilege, power, immunity. Negative (freedom from) vs positive (entitlement to).

concepts.name: obligation_legal
concepts.definition: Duty backed by enforcement. Distinct from moral obligation. Hart's rule of recognition validates.

concepts.name: sovereignty_law
concepts.definition: Ultimate legal authority. Westphalian states + internal supremacy. Increasingly contested + dispersed.

concepts.name: common_law
concepts.definition: Anglo tradition. Judge-made law through precedent. England, US, Canada, Australia, India, much of Commonwealth. Substrate analogue: substrate's case-based pattern learning.

concepts.name: civil_law_continental
concepts.definition: Roman-Germanic tradition. Codified statutes primary. France (Napoleonic Code), Germany, most of Europe, Latin America, Quebec, Louisiana. Substrate analogue: substrate's rule-based grammar.

concepts.name: religious_law
concepts.definition: Sharia (Islamic), Halakha (Jewish), Canon (Catholic). Sacred sources + interpretive traditions.

concepts.name: customary_law
concepts.definition: Indigenous + traditional. Unwritten norms backed by community. Recognised partially in many jurisdictions.

concepts.name: mixed_systems
concepts.definition: Combine traditions. Scotland (civil + common), South Africa (Roman-Dutch + common), Quebec (civil + common).

concepts.name: constitutional_law
concepts.definition: Fundamental law constituting + limiting government. Higher than ordinary statute. Judicial review (Marbury v Madison 1803).

concepts.name: criminal_law
concepts.definition: Crimes + punishment. State prosecutes. Proof beyond reasonable doubt. Mens rea + actus reus required.

concepts.name: civil_law_private
concepts.definition: Disputes between private parties. Contract + tort + property + family. Lower burden (preponderance) than criminal.

concepts.name: contract_law
concepts.definition: Enforceable agreements. Offer + acceptance + consideration. Breach + remedies (damages, specific performance).

concepts.name: tort_law
concepts.definition: Civil wrongs. Negligence + intentional + strict liability. Duty + breach + causation + damages.

concepts.name: property_law
concepts.definition: Rights in things. Bundle of sticks: possess, use, exclude, transfer, destroy. Real (land) + personal + intellectual.

concepts.name: administrative_law
concepts.definition: Government agency action. Rulemaking + adjudication. APA in US.

concepts.name: international_law
concepts.definition: Between states + IOs. Treaties + custom + general principles. Public (states) + private (cross-border transactions).

concepts.name: natural_law
concepts.definition: Aquinas + Finnis. Law's authority derived from moral truth. Unjust law no law. Lex iniusta non est lex.

concepts.name: legal_positivism
concepts.definition: Bentham, Austin, Hart, Kelsen, Raz. Law's existence + content determined by social facts, not moral merit. Separation thesis.

concepts.name: harts_concept_of_law
concepts.definition: H.L.A. Hart 1961. Primary + secondary rules. Rule of recognition validates legal system. Penumbra of uncertainty.

concepts.name: kelsen_pure_theory
concepts.definition: Hans Kelsen. Grundnorm (basic norm) validates entire hierarchy. Law as autonomous system.

concepts.name: dworkin_law_as_integrity
concepts.definition: Ronald Dworkin. Law includes principles + policies, not just rules. Right answer thesis. Hercules judge.

concepts.name: legal_realism
concepts.definition: Holmes, Llewellyn, Frank. Law is what judges do. Predicting judicial behavior, not formal rules.

concepts.name: critical_legal_studies
concepts.definition: Kennedy, Unger. Law indeterminate; reflects power. Influenced by Marxism + Frankfurt School.

concepts.name: precedent_stare_decisis
concepts.definition: Common law principle. Like cases decided alike. Binding (vertical) vs persuasive. Ratio decidendi + obiter dicta.

concepts.name: burden_of_proof
concepts.definition: Who must prove what + to what standard. Beyond reasonable doubt (criminal) > clear + convincing > preponderance (civil).

concepts.name: due_process
concepts.definition: Procedural fairness. Notice + hearing + impartial decisionmaker. Substantive due process: rights protected from arbitrary government action.

concepts.name: adversarial_system
concepts.definition: Common-law approach. Parties present, judge umpires. Vs inquisitorial (civil law) where judge investigates.

concepts.name: human_rights
concepts.definition: Universal + inalienable + indivisible. UDHR 1948 foundational. International covenants. Generation 1 (civil/political), 2 (econ/social), 3 (collective).

concepts.name: international_criminal_law
concepts.definition: Genocide + war crimes + crimes against humanity + aggression. Nuremberg + ICC.

concepts.name: law_and_economics
concepts.definition: Coase + Posner + Calabresi. Apply economic analysis to legal rules. Efficiency as criterion.

concepts.name: legal_realism_holmes
concepts.definition: Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. 'The life of the law has not been logic; it has been experience.' Predictive theory.

rules.name: law_is_union_of_primary_and_secondary_rules
rules.head: Jabberwock examines a legal system
rules.body: primary rules govern conduct; secondary rules (recognition + change + adjudication) govern the primary rules. Hart 1961. Substrate's grammar-of-grammar.

rules.name: rule_of_law_requires_specific_qualities
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates a legal regime
rules.body: Fuller's eight: prospective, general, clear, public, stable, non-contradictory, possible to comply with, applied as enacted. Substrate's well-formed-Γ conditions.

rules.name: precedent_constrains_common_law_evolution
rules.head: Jabberwock applies common law
rules.body: stare decisis: like cases decided alike. Binding precedent from superior courts. Substrate's case-based admissibility.

rules.name: burden_of_proof_allocates_uncertainty
rules.head: Jabberwock adjudicates a dispute
rules.body: burden of proof rules allocate the risk of factual uncertainty. Different standards for criminal vs civil vs administrative.

rules.name: positivism_separates_law_from_morality
rules.head: Jabberwock identifies what the law is
rules.body: law's existence + content determined by social facts (rule of recognition); legal validity does not require moral validity. Hart, Kelsen, Raz. Substrate's social-fact identification of Γ.
